description: Real E-AC-3 files: joint object coding (Dolby Atmos) test files from Dolby's Dolby Digital Plus Online Delivery Kit v1.4.1, and three E-AC-3 files from the FFmpeg sample archive: two with the adaptive hybrid transform and one with 352 bytes of junk in front. None may be redistributed here, so they are downloaded and checked against their SHA-256 rather than committed. Per file: what the analyzer, ffprobe and MediaInfo must report, the codes of the analyzer's warnings and errors ("findings") and of its infos ("info_findings"), each as a set. "archived": false marks a file the Wayback Machine has no capture of (its availability API, October 2026), so no Wayback address is listed for it.

dolby.terms: © 2018 Dolby Laboratories, Inc. All rights reserved. Dolby serves the test signals publicly for testing playback products. They are not redistributed here: CI downloads them at the pinned SHA-256 and the repository does not hold them.

ffmpeg.terms: The FFmpeg sample archive's 00-README: "You are free to download any samples you want". They are downloaded and checked, not committed.

samples.note: the file ends 32 bytes into its last 256-byte frame (6013664 is not a multiple of 256, ffprobe lists the partial packet too)
dialnorm is 0 in every frame, which A/52 5.4.2.8 reserves (MediaInfo reads it as -31 dB too); dmixmod is 3

352 bytes of junk precede the first frame, and the E-AC-3 frame headers' own bytes (from offset 6 of each frame) read as an ADTS header whose chain of three frames exists at several places; the file is E-AC-3 because the ADTS sniff asks eight frames of a chain further in and the CRC-checked E-AC-3 chain ranks 55 (ffprobe's packet count includes the junk, so no frame count is listed)
